Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Pulse-chase ATAC/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Stimulate cells briefly (e.g., TPA or serum), remove the stimulus, and profile AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and chromatin accessibility at defined time points over days. Sites that stay open after AP-1 binding has left (like the 'unpilfered' traces the word list hints at: structure remaining after the actor is gone) indicate AP-1-dependent memory, and can be compared with unstimulated controls.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation response test with AP-1 degron
ideas.description: Give a priming stimulus, rest the cells, then re-stimulate and measure transcription (RNA-seq, nascent PRO-seq) of primed versus naive cells. Use an acute degron (dTAG/auxin) on FOS/JUN either during priming only or during re-stimulation only, to separate AP-1 as the writer of memory from AP-1 as the reader.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracking of memory persistence
ideas.description: Run scRNA+scATAC with a barcoded lineage label to follow primed clones through several divisions. Test whether accessibility and gene-expression states at AP-1 motifs are inherited by daughter cells more than expected from shared environment, using sister-cell concordance and decay rates.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporters of AP-1 dynamics and target gene state
ideas.description: Image a FOS/JUN fluorescent knock-in alongside MS2/PP7 or destabilised-reporter readouts of target loci during repeated pulses. Fit a quantitative model to see whether prior pulses change the amplitude, kinetics or bistability of later responses (hysteresis), which would be the signature of memory.

ideas.title: Targeted perturbation of memory sites and AP-1 motifs
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs, or dCas9-based tools (KRAB or p300) at the sites that stay open after priming, then test whether the primed response is lost, and whether forcing the site open without AP-1 restores it. Pair this with ChIP or CUT&Tag for H3K27ac and with pioneer-factor cofactors (e.g., BAF/SWI-SNF) to find the mechanism of persistence.
